title: Former Harris County Sheriff's deputy charged with attempted sex assault while on duty: Court docs | 19898980
text:
A now-former Harris County Sheriff's deputy is facing an attempted sexual assault charge after court documents said he allegedly threatened a woman with arrest unless she performed sexual acts on him while he was on duty.

A now-former Harris County Sheriff's deputy is facing an attempted sexual assault charge after court documents said he allegedly threatened a woman with arrest unless she performed sexual acts on him while he was on duty. Court documents said in April 2025, now-former Harris County Sheriff's deputy Dohnya Dozier made that threat, and investigators said Dozier then drove the woman to a hotel room, began unbuckling his belt, but then the incident ended.
Court records also state that Dozier admitted to having sexual encounters with roughly 12 women while in uniform. Another woman, however, alleges Dozier sexually assaulted her in November 2025, and she shared her story with ABC13. Avery Daniel said the alleged assault happened Nov. 18, 2025, after she and her fiancé were involved in a domestic disturbance while staying at a Houston hotel. She said she called police, and she said Deputy Dohnya Dozier responded to the hotel.
According to Daniel, her fiancé was arrested and she was taken to a hospital. She said Dozier later arrived at the hospital. Daniel said Dozier then forced her to return to the hotel, where she alleges he sexually assaulted her. She reported the allegation to the Harris County Sheriff's Office.
In December, the sheriff's office confirmed Dozier was under investigation and had been placed on administrative leave after Daniel came forward. He has not been criminally charged in connection with Daniel's case. Daniel said she came forward because she wants to support other survivors and encourage anyone else who may have had an encounter with Dozier to report it. The Harris County Sheriff's Office said Dozier worked for the agency from July 2022 until he was fired in March 2026.
Officials are asking anyone who believes they may have been victimized by Dozier to contact them.
